title: DR1 tracks a notification through seven statuses including "Submitted action required", "Approved" and "Rejected"; the frontend has only Draft, Submitted, Amending and Deleted.

finding.frontend: A frontend notification row shows one of four tags: Draft (blue), Submitted (green), Amending (yellow) or Deleted (grey) — src/server/app/shared/kit.js:34-51 and src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:47-52. The captured row is tagged Draft. Nothing the authority does to a notification after it is received can change the tag: once submitted it reads "Submitted" for ever, and the user has no way to learn from the dashboard that something is wrong with it.
finding.prototype: DR1's dashboard tags two of its four notifications "Submitted action required" in orange and two "Submitted" in green (app/views/dashboard.html:265-292). Its status filter names the full vocabulary: Draft, Submitted, In progress, Approved, Action required, Rejected, Complete. So a DR1 notification moves through a lifecycle owned by the authority, and the dashboard is where the user finds out about it — an orange "Submitted action required" tag is the service telling the user to come back and do something.
finding.difference: The notification record needs a status that the authority can set after submission, and the dashboard needs to render it. That is a backend change first: the status today is a frontend-side lifecycle (draft, submitted, amending, deleted) with no channel for a decision coming back. Once the status arrives, map each of the seven to a tag colour and add the matching filter option. Whether "Action required" and "Submitted action required" are one status or two is worth settling before building — DR1 uses the first in its filter and the second on its cards.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a frontend notification row rendered with any status other than Draft, Submitted, Amending or Deleted.
